question: What is the main goal of cervical traction?

options.A: Massaging the deep muscle tissue
options.B: Applying a pulling force to the neck
options.C: Compressing the cervical vertebrae
options.D: Injecting fluid into the spinal space

explanation: You've got this! Cervical traction simply uses a steady, controlled pull on the neck to stretch the area and take off pressure. Easy peasy! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T12#GNS221_U1_T12_h1)

question: What are the tiny clumps of bacteria and blood clots that form on heart valves in endocarditis called?

options.A: Thromboemboli
options.B: Vegetations
options.C: Aneurysms
options.D: Atheromas

explanation: These little clumps are called vegetations. They form when germs and tiny blood clots (platelets and fibrin) stick together on a damaged heart valve. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T6#GNS213_U1_T6_h2)

question: What is the main goal of teaching pregnant women about cramps during antenatal visits?

options.A: Eliminating the need for any further doctor checkups
options.B: Instructing the mother to avoid all physical movement
options.C: Helping the patient tell normal discomforts from warning signs
options.D: Teaching the patient how to perform an ultrasound scan

explanation: Good health education helps mothers feel confident, knowing what is normal while staying alert to red flags. You're thinking like a great community nurse! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a classic sign of compartment syndrome?

options.A: Hyperactive deep tendon reflexes in the limb
options.B: Numbness and tingling sensations in the digits
options.C: Absent or very weak pulses in the affected extremity
options.D: Severe pain that does not respond to painkillers

explanation: Think of the 'Ps' of compartment syndrome: pain, pallor, pulselessness, paresthesia, and paralysis. Hyperactive reflexes don't belong on that list! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T5#GNS221_U1_T5_h6)

question: What happens if a nurse dips a needle that has already touched a patient back into a multi-dose medication vial?

options.A: The remaining fluid becomes completely neutralized
options.B: Pathogens from the patient can contaminate the entire remaining medicine
options.C: The medication instantly changes color to signal contamination
options.D: The pressure inside the glass vial drops to zero

explanation: That used needle carries tiny traces of blood and germs right into the shared bottle, turning the rest of the medication into a breeding ground for infection. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T3#GNS122_U4_T3_h3)

question: What physical feature of capillaries makes the exchange of substances possible?

options.A: Walls that are only one cell thick
options.B: Direct connections to large veins
options.C: Valves that stop blood from flowing backward
options.D: Thick muscular layers that pulse strongly

explanation: The ultra-thin single-cell wall of a capillary allows easy diffusion of gases and nutrients between blood and tissue cells. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h4)

question: Why must nurses watch for child abuse in every family, rich or poor?

options.A: Child maltreatment occurs across all backgrounds regardless of status
options.B: Wealthy families are statistically more prone to emotional abuse
options.C: Lower-income families rarely report physical injuries
options.D: Government policies mandate screening only in high-poverty areas

explanation: Abuse doesn't care about money or social class. Keep an open mind and screen everyone, no matter their background! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T24#GNS225_U5_T24_h1)

question: Why is supporting family members such an important part of critical care nursing?

options.A: Family members are legally required to perform routine nursing care tasks
options.B: Visitors help keep the unit quiet by managing other patients' alarms
options.C: Families experience high levels of stress and trauma during critical illness
options.D: Involving relatives reduces the need for expensive hospital monitoring equipment

explanation: Having a loved one in the ICU is emotionally draining for families. Being kind, clear, and supportive is a core part of caring for them too. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h9)

question: What is the best way for a nurse to ensure a patient can safely manage complex wound care and dressing changes at home?

options.A: Tell the patient to wait until the wound heals entirely on its own
options.B: Assume the family knows what to do because dressing changes are simple
options.C: Ask the patient to read a medical textbook chapter before leaving the hospital
options.D: Provide written instructions and have the patient demonstrate the technique back

explanation: Return demonstration combined with written instructions ensures the patient or caregiver actually understands and can perform the steps correctly at home. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T10#GNS213_U5_T10_h8)

question: Why should you always teach your patients the difference between a normal side effect and a dangerous adverse reaction?

options.A: It prevents panic over normal symptoms while ensuring prompt reporting of dangerous signs
options.B: It eliminates the need for any follow-up visits with the primary doctor
options.C: It guarantees the patient will never experience any drug discomfort
options.D: It allows the patient to legally prescribe their own antidote medications

explanation: Mild drowsiness is okay, but throat swelling is an emergency! Teaching the difference keeps patients calm and safe. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T6#GNS215_U4_T6_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of fructose found in seminal vesicle secretions?

options.A: It lubricates the walls of the vas deferens
options.B: It acts as a primary energy source for moving sperm
options.C: It kills harmful bacteria inside the urethra
options.D: It neutralizes the acidic environment of the vagina

explanation: Sperm use the fructose sugar secreted by the seminal vesicles to power their flagella for swimming. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T3#GNS121_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is the most common trigger for a breakthrough seizure in someone with epilepsy?

options.A: Drinking cold water
options.B: Eating too much sugar
options.C: Walking outside in bright sunlight
options.D: Missing prescribed medication doses

explanation: Consistency is key! Skipping meds lets the drug levels drop in the blood, making a seizure much more likely to happen. Remind your patients how important their schedule is. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T11#GNS222_U4_T11_h4)

question: As a student nurse, how often should you check and inspect an active peripheral IV site on your patient?

options.A: Once every 48 hours during dressing changes
options.B: Only when the patient complains of severe pain
options.C: Only when the infusion bag runs completely empty
options.D: At least once every nursing shift

explanation: Exactly! Regular checks each shift help you catch tiny problems like early swelling or soreness before they turn into bigger issues. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T6#GNS311_U4_T6_h7)

question: What is a very common blood sugar issue caused by severe stress in critically ill patients?

options.A: Decreased metabolic demand
options.B: Rapid spontaneous weight loss
options.C: Stress-induced hyperglycemia
options.D: Severe chronic hypokalemia

explanation: When the body goes through severe stress or trauma, it releases hormones that often shoot blood sugar levels right up. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a classic warning sign of a growing ovarian tumor?

options.A: Urinary urgency or frequency
options.B: Unexplained weight gain in the upper arms
options.C: Persistent abdominal bloating
options.D: Feeling full very quickly after starting a meal

explanation: Correct! Upper arm weight gain is not linked to ovarian tumors, but bloating, feeling full fast, and rushing to the toilet are classic signs. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T33#GNS216_U5_T33_h4)

question: In which direction should you smooth a topical lotion onto a patient's skin?

options.A: Strictly from the bottom of the limb upward
options.B: In a crisscross pattern across the rash
options.C: In the direction of hair growth
options.D: In tight circular motions against the hair

explanation: Smoothing lotions in the direction of hair growth keeps hair follicles happy and prevents painful inflammation. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T20#GNS122_U1_T20_h7)

question: What is the primary job of the large intestine in the human body?

options.A: Digesting complex fats and proteins
options.B: Filtering waste products out of the blood stream
options.C: Producing most of the body's digestive enzymes
options.D: Absorbing water and forming stool

explanation: The main function of the colon is to take liquid chyme from the small intestine, absorb the water and electrolytes, and turn it into solid feces. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h1)

question: Which contraceptive category offers protection against both pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: Subdermal implants
options.B: Barrier methods
options.C: Copper intrauterine devices
options.D: Progestin mini-pills

explanation: Barrier methods like condoms physically block bodily fluids, thereby preventing the transmission of infectious organisms as well as sperm. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T17#GNS215_U6_T17_h5)

question: How do uterine contractions help during a medical abortion?

options.A: They push the gestational sac down and out through the dilated cervix
options.B: They raise blood pressure to flush out toxins
options.C: They permanently numb pelvic nerves so there is zero pain
options.D: They seal off the uterine lining to stop hormones

explanation: Once the cervix is soft, those rhythmic uterine contractions create the gentle pressure needed to clear the pregnancy tissue safely. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T013#GNS226_U5_T013_h2)

question: What are the two main types of data collected during a cardiovascular assessment?

options.A: Physical and diagnostic data
options.B: Primary and secondary data
options.C: Internal and external data
options.D: Subjective and objective data

explanation: Subjective data comes from what the patient tells you, while objective data comes from what you measure and observe directly. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T2#GNS213_U1_T2_h1)

question: What does 'hidden hunger' mean in community nutrition?

options.A: Eating enough calories from starchy foods while lacking vital micronutrients
options.B: A sudden shortage of food caused by severe drought conditions
options.C: A psychological condition where patients refuse to eat despite starving
options.D: The physical sensation of hunger felt late at night

explanation: Exactly! Hidden hunger happens when someone gets enough food to fill their stomach (like heavy swallows of starch), but their diet misses the key vitamins and minerals they really need. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T17#GNS214_U1_T17_h2)

question: Which clinical sign tells you that an antibiotic is successfully beating the infection?

options.A: Elevation in patient blood pressure readings
options.B: Complete disappearance of normal skin flora
options.C: Increase in patient appetite within one hour
options.D: Reduction in fever and white blood cell count

explanation: Brilliant! Watching the fever drop and WBC count return to normal is a classic nursing win. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T2#GNS215_U6_T2_h7)

question: What is the normal reference range for arterial carbon dioxide ($PaCO_2$)?

options.A: 22 to 26 mmHg
options.B: 80 to 100 mmHg
options.C: 7.35 to 7.45 mmHg
options.D: 35 to 45 mmHg

explanation: Keep this handy normal value in mind: arterial $CO_2$ normally sits right between 35 and 45 mmHg. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T13#GNS121_U2_T13_h7)

question: How do authorities decide if a substance is legally classified as hazardous waste?

options.A: By measuring how heavy the shipping container is when loaded onto a truck
options.B: By testing whether the material dissolves easily in clean drinking water
options.C: By checking if the manufacturing company is publicly traded on the stock market
options.D: By looking at its specific waste stream source or dangerous characteristics

explanation: Spot on! The treaty looks at where the waste came from and how it behaves (like if it's toxic or flammable) to classify it properly. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h4)

question: Why is prioritization necessary after collecting community health data?

options.A: Government regulations forbid treating more than one disease at a time
options.B: Minor health issues are completely unimportant and should be ignored forever
options.C: It helps nurses avoid doing any field work for the rest of the year
options.D: Resources like time and money are limited, so the most urgent issues must be tackled first

explanation: Because resources are finite, prioritization ensures the most pressing and impactful health problems receive attention first. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h6)

question: What is the main job of hCG (the pregnancy hormone) in the early weeks?

options.A: To signal the corpus luteum to keep making progesterone
options.B: To trigger the immediate production of mature breast milk
options.C: To lower maternal blood pressure to prevent hypertension
options.D: To soften the pelvic ligaments for upcoming delivery

explanation: Spot on! hCG tells the body's temporary structure (the corpus luteum) to stay put and keep pumping out progesterone to keep the pregnancy safe. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T14#GNS121_U5_T14_h2)

question: When a mum gets admitted to the labour ward, why is checking her antenatal card so important?

options.A: To determine the exact time the baby will be born
options.B: To find out if the mother attended antenatal classes regularly
options.C: To identify pre-existing risk factors and review past test results
options.D: To calculate the hospital bill for the delivery service

explanation: Her antenatal card holds secrets to a safe delivery! It shows her blood group, scan results, and any risks we need to watch out for. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T002#GNS226_U3_T002_h3)

question: How does high resistance in the body's blood vessels affect the heart?

options.A: It stops electrical impulses from reaching the lower heart chambers
options.B: It increases afterload, making it harder for the heart to push blood out
options.C: It lowers the heart rate by relaxing the nervous system
options.D: It decreases preload by trapping extra fluid inside the lungs

explanation: When blood vessels are tight, the heart has to work much harder to push blood past them. That extra workload is called afterload! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T12#GNS213_U1_T12_h1)

question: What crucial advice should a nurse give a patient taking antibiotics for endometritis?

options.A: Take the pills only when pelvic pain becomes severe
options.B: Double the dose if a single pill is accidentally missed
options.C: Finish the entire prescription even if symptoms improve
options.D: Stop taking the medication as soon as the fever drops

explanation: Always remind patients to finish their drugs! Stopping early lets the strongest surviving bacteria bounce back, causing a relapse or drug resistance. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T20#GNS216_U5_T20_h7)

question: Why must a nurse know the exact landmarks of the vulva?

options.A: To pass a urinary catheter without missing the urethra
options.B: To prevent ovarian cysts
options.C: To measure blood pressure correctly
options.D: To track the exact day of ovulation

explanation: Spot on! Knowing your anatomy keeps procedures safe and stops you from accidentally placing a catheter into the vaginal opening instead of the urethra. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T2#GNS311_U1_T2_h1)

question: Where is sodium mostly found in the body, making it a key electrolyte?

options.A: Neutral protein molecule
options.B: Fat-soluble vitamin
options.C: Intracellular fluid (inside cells)
options.D: Extracellular fluid (outside cells)

explanation: You've got this! Sodium is a positively charged ion that stays mostly in the fluid outside of our cells, which is why it's called an extracellular cation. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h2)

question: What symptom is most characteristic of gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GORD)?

options.A: Chronic constipation
options.B: Severe right shoulder pain
options.C: Heartburn
options.D: Projectile vomiting of blood

explanation: You've got it! Heartburn—that burning discomfort right behind your breastbone caused by acid irritation—is the classic hallmark of GORD. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T5#GNS213_U3_T5_h2)

question: Which of these makes a topical medication much more likely to absorb into the bloodstream and cause toxicity?

options.A: Washing the skin thoroughly with mild soap and water
options.B: Applying the cream over large areas of broken skin
options.C: Rotating the application site with every dose
options.D: Using a clean tongue depressor to spread the ointment

explanation: When skin is broken, its natural protective barrier is gone, letting too much medicine flood into the bloodstream. Good clinical awareness! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T9#GNS122_U1_T9_h6)

question: What triggers the release of oxytocin during breastfeeding?

options.A: High levels of circulating estrogen
options.B: Emptying of the axillary lymph nodes
options.C: Stretching of Cooper's ligaments
options.D: Infant suckling at the nipple

explanation: Nerve signals from the nipple travel to the brain when a baby suckles, triggering the posterior pituitary to release oxytocin for milk ejection. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T16#GNS121_U5_T16_h8)

question: Why is calming a patient's emotions just as important as treating their physical wounds in a crisis?

options.A: It completely erases the memory of the traumatic event
options.B: It speeds up the hospital discharge process for all patients
options.C: It prevents the physical injuries from becoming infected
options.D: It lowers acute stress and supports physical healing

explanation: Great thinking! When we help patients calm down, their stress hormones drop, making it much easier for their bodies to heal and for them to work with us. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T9#GNS112_U7_T9_h1)

question: Which structure forms the roof of the mouth and separates it from the nasal cavity?

options.A: The lips and cheeks
options.B: The tongue and floor muscles
options.C: The hard and soft palates
options.D: The fauces and uvula

explanation: The hard palate and soft palate together make up the roof of the mouth, creating a firm barrier between the oral and nasal cavities. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T1#GNS121_U1_T1_h2)

question: What is a main duty of a nurse working in a school?

options.A: Purchasing food supplies for the school cafeteria
options.B: Conducting routine health screenings and managing minor injuries
options.C: Setting the financial budget for local education ministries
options.D: Designing the structural blueprints for new school buildings

explanation: Exactly! School nurses focus on first aid, checking students' health, and handling everyday health needs right on campus. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h3)

question: What is the teach-back method used for during patient education?

options.A: Writing prescription notes for the pharmacist
options.B: Asking the patient to explain the information back in their own words
options.C: Having the nurse read the textbook out loud to the patient
options.D: Testing the nurse's ability to memorize medical terminology

explanation: The teach-back method checks whether the patient truly understood the instructions by having them repeat the information. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h5)

question: What kind of thinking or belief is a classic sign of a patient with GPI?

options.A: Hearing strangers whispering secrets all day
options.B: Washing their hands constantly out of fear of germs
options.C: Being terrified of open spaces
options.D: Grandiose delusions, like believing they own the whole world

explanation: That's right! Patients with GPI often have huge, unrealistic beliefs about themselves, such as thinking they are multi-millionaires, royalty, or even gods. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T1#GNS222_U4_T1_h3)

question: How can you best help a patient with a tracheostomy tube who temporarily cannot speak?

options.A: Temporarily remove parts of the tube
options.B: Provide writing pads or communication boards
options.C: Tell them to whisper to keep their voice strong
options.D: Ask only yes-or-no questions for head nods

explanation: Spot on! Alternative tools like writing boards let patients express themselves clearly without straining or irritating their airway. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T5#GNS213_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is a common emotional response experienced by a person who has recently acquired a permanent physical disability?

options.A: Complete indifference toward their physical health status
options.B: Immediate and permanent acceptance of the new lifestyle
options.C: Euphoria over lifestyle changes and reduced responsibilities
options.D: Grief and a process similar to mourning a loss

explanation: Patients frequently experience a grief reaction as they process the loss of their previous physical abilities and independence. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T9#GNS225_U5_T9_h6)

question: A patient with severe bipolar disorder is having a manic episode with racing thoughts. Which medication type is most helpful to include?

options.A: A broad-spectrum antibiotic
options.B: A short-acting multivitamin
options.C: An oral iron supplement
options.D: An atypical antipsychotic

explanation: You'll often see doctors prescribe atypical antipsychotics alongside mood stabilizers to quickly calm down acute mania in bipolar disorder. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T6#GNS223_U6_T6_h5)

question: Which organ is in the greatest danger during a paracetamol overdose?

options.A: The stomach
options.B: The kidneys
options.C: The liver
options.D: The pancreas

explanation: The liver works hard to break down paracetamol. When too much is taken at once, it gets overwhelmed and can suffer serious damage. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T2#GNS223_U5_T2_h2)

question: How can you easily tell the difference between a vesicle and a bulla?

options.A: A vesicle contains pus while a bulla contains clear serum only
options.B: A vesicle appears on mucous membranes while a bulla appears on nails
options.C: A vesicle is smaller than 1 cm while a bulla is larger than 1 cm
options.D: A vesicle is solid and raised while a bulla is completely flat

explanation: Both are fluid-filled blisters! The only real difference is their size—bullae are just the bigger ones over 1 cm. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T8#GNS213_U5_T8_h2)

question: What is considered the absolute best (gold standard) way to confirm a nasogastric tube is in the right spot?

options.A: Measuring the length of tubing left outside the nose
options.B: Listening for air sounds over the belly with a stethoscope
options.C: Checking for water drops inside the clear plastic tube
options.D: Abdominal X-ray

explanation: An X-ray gives us clear visual proof that the tip is sitting comfortably in the stomach before we start any feeding. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T2#GNS212_U1_T2_h5)

question: Why do advanced tumors often become resistant to medical treatments like chemotherapy?

options.A: The body's immune system destroys the medication before it reaches the tumor
options.B: Chemotherapy drugs turn normal cells into malignant cancer cells
options.C: Genetic diversity creates varied cell populations with different drug resistance traits
options.D: Tumor cells develop a protective bone shell that blocks all medications

explanation: As mutations accumulate, cancer cells become diverse; while some cells die from treatment, resistant clones survive and multiply. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is the golden rule of nursing documentation when it comes to legal protection?

options.A: If it was not charted, it was not done
options.B: Only write down abnormal patient vitals
options.C: Always erase mistakes with correction fluid
options.D: Chart at the end of the week from memory

explanation: In the eyes of the law, if you didn't write it down in the chart, it never happened. Document everything you do! [learn more](GST321_U10_T7#GST321_U10_T7_h7)

question: What type of drug is given to clear away any lingering strep bacteria in these patients?

options.A: Anticoagulants
options.B: Bronchodilators
options.C: Antipyretics
options.D: Antibiotics

explanation: We use antibiotics like penicillin to wipe out any stubborn strep bacteria still hiding in the body. Spot on! [learn more](GNS213_U4_T4#GNS213_U4_T4_h6)

question: What is the main goal of performing a vulvar swab?

options.A: To measure the internal pH of the vaginal canal accurately
options.B: To collect microbial samples from the external female genitalia
options.C: To empty residual fluid from the urinary bladder completely
options.D: To remove excess tissue growth from the labia minora safely

explanation: You've got this! A vulvar swab is simply used to collect samples from the outside parts to find out what germ is causing issues like itching or unusual discharge. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h1)

question: Which part of the female reproductive system is mainly affected in endometritis?

options.A: The inner lining of the uterus
options.B: The lower part of the birth canal
options.C: The outer covering of the ovaries
options.D: The muscular wall of the womb

explanation: You've got this! 'Endo' means inside, and 'metritis' relates to the uterus. So endometritis is simply an infection or inflammation of the inner lining of the womb (the endometrium). [learn more](GNS216_U5_T20#GNS216_U5_T20_h1)

question: Which imaging scan is commonly used to stage lymphomas by checking for swollen lymph nodes?

options.A: Pulmonary function test
options.B: Computed tomography (CT) scan
options.C: Electroencephalogram (EEG)
options.D: Electrocardiogram (ECG)

explanation: A CT scan gives clear, slice-by-slice pictures that show the size and location of lymph nodes and organs inside the body. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T5#GNS311_U2_T5_h7)

question: What does cloudy cerebrospinal fluid usually tell the medical team?

options.A: Presence of excess oxygen in the brain
options.B: High levels of dietary sugar in the blood
options.C: Presence of white blood cells from infection
options.D: Normal aging process of the nervous system

explanation: Well done! Cloudiness usually means white blood cells are crowded in there fighting off an infection like meningitis. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T11#GNS222_U3_T11_h7)

question: What type of energy does an MRI scanner use to produce diagnostic images?

options.A: Radioactive tracer isotopes
options.B: Ionizing radiation waves
options.C: High-frequency sound waves
options.D: Magnetic fields and radiofrequency

explanation: MRI uses powerful magnets and radiofrequency waves rather than harmful radiation to create detailed pictures of the body. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T7#GNS222_U1_T7_h1)

question: Prolonged pressure from the baby's head against the bladder during difficult labour can lead to which lasting complication?

options.A: Gestational hypertension
options.B: Vesicovaginal fistula
options.C: Chronic pelvic inflammatory disease
options.D: Placenta previa

explanation: This is a key one in midwifery practice. Continuous pressure cuts off blood flow to the bladder wall, forming an opening (fistula) that causes constant urine leakage. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h4)

question: Which symptom is a major red flag for intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy?

options.A: Painful blisters forming exclusively around the mouth
options.B: Rapid darkening of the skin over the entire body
options.C: Severe itching on the palms and soles without an initial rash
options.D: Thick crusting sores spreading across the scalp

explanation: Take note of this one for the ward! Intense itching on hands and feet without a rash can mean liver acid backup (cholestasis) and needs quick medical attention. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h5)

question: What does 'test-retest reliability' check in a study?

options.A: Stability of scores over time
options.B: Agreement between two different observers
options.C: Equivalence of two different questionnaire versions
options.D: Internal similarity of survey questions

explanation: Spot on! Test-retest simply means giving the same test to the same people at two different times to see if the scores stay stable. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T27#GNS224_U1_T27_h3)

question: Why do we give a routine Vitamin K injection to all healthy newborns?

options.A: To protect against neonatal eye infections
options.B: To prevent hemorrhagic disease of the newborn
options.C: To boost immediate immunological antibody counts
options.D: To stimulate the production of brown fat cells

explanation: Babies are born with sterile tummies and can't make their own Vitamin K yet. Giving this shot protects them from dangerous bleeding until their gut matures. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T014#GNS226_U3_T014_h3)

question: Why is 'Risk for Infection' a top concern when a patient's white blood cell count is low?

options.A: The patient is forced to share a room with other sick individuals
options.B: The body lacks sufficient defense mechanisms to fight off invading pathogens
options.C: Intravenous lines always cause immediate blood infections
options.D: Hospital linens usually harbor resistant bacterial strains

explanation: White blood cells are our frontline soldiers against germs. When numbers are down, even friendly germs can become a big problem. Protection is key! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T13#GNS311_U2_T13_h3)

question: Why is it important to get feedback quickly after a test or practical?

options.A: To guarantee you graduate with first-class honors
options.B: To reduce the amount of work for your clinical tutor
options.C: So you can fix bad habits before they stick
options.D: So you never feel anxious about clinicals again

explanation: Quick feedback stops a wrong practice from turning into a dangerous habit. The sooner you know your error, the faster you can master the right way! [learn more](GST321_U9_T2#GST321_U9_T2_h4)

question: Why is regular cleaning and disinfecting of bed accessories so important in the ward?

options.A: To keep the equipment looking brand new for visitors
options.B: To make the rubber and plastic components softer
options.C: To prevent the metal parts from rusting too quickly
options.D: To prevent the spread of hospital-acquired infections

explanation: Spot on! Since bed accessories are often shared, wiping them down thoroughly between patients stops germs from spreading and keeps everyone safe. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T4#GNS112_U4_T4_h6)

question: A patient needs a morning blood test for specific hormone levels. What is the best nursing action?

question: What is the main purpose of a health screening test?

question: What is the correct way to feel (palpate) lymph nodes during a physical exam?

question: How does pelvic floor physical therapy help treat genito-pelvic pain?

options.C: It increases systemic testosterone production instantly
options.D: It relaxes and conditions hypertonic pelvic muscles

question: A patient with a stroke in the front of the pons is fully awake and alert, but cannot speak or move their body below the neck. What is this called?

options.C: Wernicke encephalopathy

question: What is the main focus of a servant leader in nursing?

options.A: Prioritizing the growth and well-being of the healthcare team

options.C: Avoiding all interaction with junior nursing personnel

question: What is a major perk of getting your vitamins from real food instead of pills?

options.C: Whole foods cost nothing at all to produce or purchase

question: Why are health and learning considered intertwined in school health philosophy?

options.B: Schools get extra funding for running clinics

question: At what angle should you insert the needle for an intradermal injection?

question: What is the primary job of an ascending spinal tract?

options.C: Producing cerebrospinal fluid in the spinal canal

question: Why do people easily fall for popular food trends?

question: What is the term for permanent brain damage caused by untreated severe neonatal jaundice?

question: Why do doctors often order a transvaginal ultrasound when a patient has abnormal bleeding?

question: What role does regular feedback play in the philosophy of MBO?

question: What is the recommended period of sexual abstinence before providing a semen sample for analysis?

question: A 30-week pregnant woman comes to the clinic complaining of a severe headache and blurred vision. What is your very first nursing action?

question: How often should you check mum's vital signs and uterus during her very first hour after delivery?

options.D: Every 15 minutes

explanation: That first hour is high-alert time for postpartum hemorrhage. Frequent 15-minute checks let you catch any sneaky bleeding early. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T008#GNS226_U3_T008_h9)

question: A patient tells you they feel extremely panicked and short of breath at the thought of entering a narrow, enclosed scanner. What is your best first action?

question: Why do lipid-soluble (steroid) hormones need carrier proteins to travel through the blood?

question: How do daily pill organizers help improve patient medication adherence?

question: At an antenatal clinic in Nigeria, a pregnant woman receives sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine. What is this for?

question: Where is the safest place to give a vitamin K injection to a full-term newborn?

question: What is the main goal of adolescent-friendly health services?

question: Why is post-test counselling still very important for someone who tests negative?

question: Why must body tissues and human parts be separated from normal general waste?

question: Why do nurses use audience segmentation when planning a health intervention?

question: A nurse listens with a stethoscope and hears moist, popping sounds at the lung bases of a patient with heart failure. What are these sounds called?

question: A patient taking furosemide feels dizzy and lightheaded when standing up quickly. What is the most likely reason?

question: Why are interdisciplinary rounds (where different health workers meet together) so helpful?

question: Why is it important to ask about past surgical complications, such as a bad reaction to anesthesia?

question: What is the main purpose of following clinical protocols in nursing practice?

question: What is a key sign that a post-abortion patient might be in severe pain?

question: Which of these is a foundational lifestyle change for managing hypertension?

question: What are the three parts of the small intestine in order, starting right after the stomach?

question: When we talk about 'somatosensation', what kind of feelings are we including?

question: What early signs do women with ovarian cancer most often report to their doctors?

question: Which of these is a very common trigger that makes pregnancy nausea worse?

question: Why might a patient with very low white blood cells (neutropenia) NOT show classic signs of infection like pus?

question: Why does the PMTCT strategy include primary prevention of HIV in women as its first prong?

question: What are the three main signs of professional burnout in healthcare workers?

question: Why do patients who had a myxoma removed still need occasional follow-up scans?

question: Which of these is a common physical sign of andropause?

question: What is a pathologic fracture?

question: What is the main goal of medications called inotropes in acute heart failure?

question: What protective gear is a must-have when preparing cytotoxic drugs?

question: Why do pre-existing medical conditions often get worse during pregnancy?

question: Why must every item inside the home visiting kit have a specific, designated place?

question: Why do standard health programs sometimes fail when trying to help marginalized groups?

question: Why is early recognition of genitourinary growths so important?

question: Why should a patient empty their bladder before a physical examination?

question: Why do we encourage families to plan emergency transport before the baby arrives?

question: Which layer of the uterus is shed monthly during menstruation?

question: Why is food safety especially important for individuals living with HIV?

options.C: To warm up the medication liquid inside the glass container

explanation: Wiping the access port with alcohol reduces surface bacteria and prevents introducing pathogens into sterile solutions. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T2#GNS125_U4_T2_h6)

question: A patient with Korsakoff syndrome insists on going home to feed a pet dog that died years ago. How should you respond?

options.A: Agree that the dog is waiting at home for them
options.B: Gently redirect the patient to a current activity without arguing
options.C: Ignore the patient and leave the room immediately
options.D: Argue firmly until the patient admits the dog is dead

explanation: Arguing will only upset or confuse them. The kindest nursing move is to stay calm, validate their feelings softly, and smoothly guide them to a new activity. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T8#GNS222_U4_T8_h8)

question: A nurse prepares an exact dose of an injectable drug and saves the remainder carefully. What good nursing practice does this show?

options.A: Unnecessary creation of pathological waste
options.B: Improper sharps disposal technique
options.C: A direct breach of universal safety laws
options.D: Waste reduction and efficient resource use

explanation: Well done! Careful dosing avoids unnecessary surplus that would otherwise end up being thrown away. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h3)

question: How do pelvic floor exercises help patients recovering from GU cancer treatments?

options.A: They increase testosterone production in the testes
options.B: They strengthen muscles to help regain bladder control
options.C: They improve the filtration rate of the renal cortex
options.D: They prevent the recurrence of cancerous cell growth

explanation: Pelvic floor exercises (like Kegels) tone up the muscles supporting the bladder and urethra, which is a huge help for clients dealing with leakage after surgery. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h8)

question: What happens when 'noise' or interference enters the communication process?

options.A: It speeds up how fast the sender talks to the receiver
options.B: It disrupts the message and can lead to misunderstandings
options.C: It changes the communication channel into a written format
options.D: It automatically guarantees the client will follow instructions

explanation: Noise represents any barrier or distraction that gets in the way of clear message transmission between sender and receiver. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h2)

question: Which infection is most directly linked to the development of cervical cancer?

options.A: Neisseria gonorrhoeae
options.B: Human papillomavirus
options.C: Chlamydia trachomatis
options.D: Human immunodeficiency virus

explanation: High-risk strains of human papillomavirus (HPV) can hang around in the cells of the cervix for years and eventually cause cell changes that lead to cancer. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T12#GNS311_U1_T12_h7)

question: What is the primary function of the large intestine?

options.A: To absorb water and electrolytes from indigestible food residue
options.B: To produce bile salts needed for fat emulsification
options.C: To begin the mechanical breakdown of ingested food
options.D: To secrete strong acids and enzymes for protein digestion

explanation: The large intestine reclaims most of the remaining water, converting liquid waste into formed stool. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T6#GNS121_U1_T6_h7)

question: A patient drinks a six-ounce cup of juice. How many milliliters should the nurse record on the chart?

options.A: 60 milliliters
options.B: 180 milliliters
options.C: 300 milliliters
options.D: 120 milliliters

explanation: Multiplying six ounces by thirty milliliters per ounce gives a total volume of 180 milliliters. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T19#GNS122_U1_T19_h6)

question: What is the single best way to prevent a catheter-associated urinary tract infection (CAUTI)?

options.A: Clamp the catheter for two hours every afternoon
options.B: Remove the catheter as soon as it is no longer medically necessary
options.C: Apply antibiotic ointment around the meatus three times a day
options.D: Disconnect the drainage tubing every morning to flush it out

explanation: You've got it! The golden rule of preventing catheter infections is taking the tube out the moment it's no longer needed. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T21#GNS212_U1_T21_h7)

question: What major global health crisis drove the rapid development of early mechanical ventilation?

options.A: The polio epidemics of the mid-20th century
options.B: The 1918 influenza pandemic across Europe
options.C: Major outbreaks of cholera in crowded cities
options.D: The rapid rise of severe traumatic road accidents

explanation: The polio epidemics caused widespread respiratory paralysis, forcing hospitals to find mechanical ways to help patients breathe. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h2)

question: A patient takes painkillers for joint pain every day and suddenly complains of a burning stomach. What's the most likely cause?

options.A: A normal reaction that requires no further action
options.B: An allergic reaction causing skin rashes
options.C: Gastric irritation from anti-inflammatory drugs
options.D: A complete blockage of the large intestine

explanation: Common pain meds (like NSAIDs) can wear down the protective lining of the stomach, leading to irritation and burning pain. Good to watch out for in clinical practice! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T2#GNS213_U3_T2_h2)

question: What is the purpose of recommending pelvic floor exercises in the long-term recovery phase?

options.A: To help restore and strengthen anal sphincter tone
options.B: To speed up the healing of abdominal skin scars
options.C: To increase the production of digestive enzymes
options.D: To prevent the development of high blood pressure

explanation: Strengthening the pelvic floor muscles improves overall continence and pelvic support after surgery. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h9)

question: Which compress is best for a patient who twisted their ankle just ten minutes ago?

options.A: Alternating hot and steaming compress
options.B: Room-temperature dry wrap
options.C: Cold compress
options.D: Warm compress

explanation: For fresh injuries (acute injuries), cold therapy is your best friend to keep swelling and pain down. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T9#GNS221_U3_T9_h2)
